roasters.name: 12 Knots Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: 12 Knots Coffee Roasters is a family business in Trollhättan run by Jihyeon ‘LJ’ Lee, originally from South Korea, and Amelie Länsberg Lee. The business began with small-scale roasting and coffee tastings before establishing a physical presence in Trollhättan.

image.alt: Roastery image for 12 Knots Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Ala rosteri
roasters.description: Ala Rosteri is a family-run roastery on the countryside outside Laholm. Johan and Mel built the roastery in a converted farm building, making the business closely tied to the family property where production takes place.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Ask Kafferosteri
roasters.description: Ask Kafferosteri is a Torslanda roastery founded by Leonard, a former pilot who moved from personal coffee interest and small roasting experiments into running a local roasting business. The company grew directly out of those home-scale experiments.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Balck Coffee
roasters.description: Balck Coffee is a Kalmar-based roastery founded by Sebastian Balck in 2016. The idea grew from his experience of Italian coffee-bar culture, and the business began on a small scale in Kalmar before developing into a local roasting company.

image.alt: Balck Coffee logo with turquoise leaves.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Beanaut Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Beanaut Coffee Roasters is based in Örebro and was founded in spring 2022 by Rafal Walczak and Niklas Andersson. The company was created as a small roasting operation centred on selected specialty coffees and has built its identity around roasting for coffee enthusiasts.

image.alt: Roastery image for Beanaut Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Bergstrands Kafferosteri
roasters.description: Bergstrands Kafferosteri is a Gothenburg roastery with roots going back to 1891. The company is family-owned and is now run by the fifth generation, making it one of Sweden’s older continuously operated coffee businesses. Its present production combines that long roasting history with a modern roasting facility and a broad range of coffees.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Big Lake Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Big Lake Coffee Roasters is based in Östersund and is strongly associated with Jämtland. The business operates as a modern local roastery selling roasted coffee directly to consumers. Kaffefolk AB is registered at the same address and appears to be closely connected to the current operating structure.

image.alt: Roastery image for Big Lake Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Björklunds Kafferosteri
roasters.description: Björklunds Kafferosteri is based in Västerås, where the company roasts and sells its own coffee from its premises on Slakterigatan. The business is an established independent Swedish roaster with both consumer sales and a broader commercial customer base.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Blakk kafferosteri
roasters.description: Blakk Kafferosteri is a small roastery based in Stenungsund on Sweden’s west coast. The company sells its own roasted coffee through its website and local channels.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Blekinge Coffee
roasters.description: Blekinge Coffee is based in Mörrum and is run by Henrik Arvidsson. Arvidsson handles the roasting operation and works with seasonal coffee purchases, documented roast batches and systematic cupping as part of the company’s day-to-day production.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Borås kafferosteri
roasters.description: Borås Kafferosteri is a small roasting company based in Borås. It operates its own local roasting business and sells coffee under the Borås Kafferosteri name.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Budhas kafferosteri
roasters.description: Budhas Kafferosteri is a micro-roastery based in Lycksele. It operates as a local independent roaster with its own webshop and a range centred on specialty coffee.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Cafégo
roasters.description: Cafégo is a Swedish coffee brand whose roasting operation has changed structure in recent years. From 2026 the current operator is Gårdens Rosteri & Skafferi AB in Trelleborg; the previous operating company was Sofiero Kafferosteri AB. The brand therefore has roots in the earlier Sofiero roasting business while continuing under a new legal operator.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Coffea Circulor
roasters.description: Coffea Circulor is a Gothenburg-based specialty coffee project associated with Ivica Cvetanovski. The business has become known for an unusually experimental and technical approach to coffee selection, processing and brewing, with a strong emphasis on detailed producer and lot information.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Costas of Sweden
roasters.description: Costas of Sweden is a Umeå-based roastery built by Costas Pliatsikas after years of work with coffee and barista competitions. He established his own roasting operation in 2006 and became Swedish Barista Champion in 2007. The company has since remained closely associated with Umeå’s specialty-coffee scene.

image.alt: Roastery image for Costas of Sweden.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Cozo Coffee
roasters.description: Cozo Coffee was founded in Örebro in 2017 by Oskar Cedermalm. Cedermalm came to the business with a background that also included work as a touring musician, and built Cozo as a small independent roastery specialising in carefully selected coffees.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: da Matteo
roasters.description: da Matteo is a Gothenburg coffee company with its own roasting operation alongside its cafés and bakery activities. It has become one of the city’s best-known independent coffee businesses and roasts coffee for both its own venues and external customers.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Drop Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Drop Coffee is a Stockholm-based roastery founded in 2009 as a coffee bar near Mariatorget. The company began roasting coffee in the back of the café in 2010 on a one-kilo roaster, before moving production to a dedicated facility in 2012. In 2018 the roastery relocated to Rosersberg, north of Stockholm, while the original café remained at Mariatorget. Drop is owned and operated by Joanna Alm Leighton and Stephen Leighton. Joanna Alm is a three-time Swedish Coffee Roasting Champion and has placed second in the World Coffee Roasting Championship.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Fandango Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Fandango Coffee Roasters is a Swedish roastery launched in Stockholm in 2026 after its founders had spent nearly ten years working in the coffee industry across several countries. The company combines coffee roasting with a distinctive visual interest in medieval, baroque and antique aesthetics. Its legal company is registered in Bålsta, and it sells seasonal coffees and subscriptions directly online.

image.alt: Roastery image for Fandango Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Fika Moose kafferosteri
roasters.description: Fika Moose Kafferosteri is a small roastery based in Lerdala outside Skövde. It operates as a local roasting business with direct consumer sales and an online presence.

image.alt: Roastery image for Fika Moose kafferosteri.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Gamla Snickeriet kafferosteri
roasters.description: Gamla Snickeriet Kafferosteri is a small coffee roastery in Säter. The business operates under the Gamla Snickeriet name and roasts coffee locally for direct sale.

image.alt: Roastery image for Gamla Snickeriet kafferosteri.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Gringo Nordic Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Gringo Nordic is a Gothenburg-based roastery founded in 2018 by Johan Ekfeldt. Ekfeldt had previously worked for Kahls and co-founded Johan & Nyström in 2004 before later returning to roasting with Gringo. He runs the company together with Pernilla Ekfeldt and the wider team in western Gothenburg. The business also operates a coffee bar and shop alongside the roastery.

image.alt: Blue and red Gringo Nordic coffee bags.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Gute rosteri
roasters.description: Gute Rosteri is a Gotland-based coffee roastery operating from Barlingbo, with additional café and serving activities on the island. The business combines local roasting with a broader hospitality presence on Gotland.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Gåshaga kafferosteri
roasters.description: Gåshaga Kafferosteri is based on Lidingö. The business grew out of a company background in Nordic video and retail before moving into coffee concepts and eventually building its own roasting operation. That unusual route from retail into coffee remains a distinctive part of the company’s history.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Hälla kafferosteri
roasters.description: Hälla Kafferosteri was founded in Västerås in 2019 by brothers Kaj and Dan Johdet. Their path into roasting followed earlier barista experience and an encounter with coffee roasting in 2017. The company roasts exclusively specialty coffee.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: I am Coffee
roasters.description: I am Coffee is a Halmstad-based roastery founded by Alpha Ousmane Sow. Sow has roots in Guinea-Conakry and comes from a family with a background in coffee farming. Parts of the company’s coffee offering are connected to farms linked to his own family and origin.

image.alt: Roastery image for I am Coffee.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Ingarö rosteri
roasters.description: Ingarö Rosteri was founded on Ingarö in the Stockholm archipelago in 2010. Roasting, packing and distribution are carried out from the island, giving the business a distinctly local production model.

image.alt: Ingarö Rosteri logo with a coffee cup.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Johan & Nyström
roasters.description: Johan & Nyström was founded in 2004 and became one of the early Swedish companies to build a business around specialty coffee, roasting and coffee education. The company later became part of the Espresso House group in 2016. Its roasting operation in Länna also supplies coffee within the wider group.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Järna rosteri
roasters.description: Järna Rosteri is a small independent roastery based in Järna south of Stockholm. The company roasts coffee locally and sells under its own name.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: K&B kafferosteri
roasters.description: K&B Kafferosteri is a small independent roastery based in Laholm. It operates its own roasting business and sells coffee directly under the K&B name.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: K.W. Karlberg kafferosteri
roasters.description: K.W. Karlberg Kafferosteri traces its history to Karl Wilhelm Karlberg, who started the business in 1890. The company has continued through several generations and periods of Swedish coffee history, making it one of the older names in the database.

image.alt: Roastery image for K.W. Karlberg kafferosteri.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kaffemissionären
roasters.description: Kaffemissionären is a Stockholm coffee project founded by Viktor Liljerås. The business was created around buying and roasting specialty coffee, with a stated aim of directing more of the value in the coffee chain toward producers.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kaffero
roasters.description: Kaffero is a small roastery in Hallsberg run by Noa and Markus. They built the company around roasting their own coffee locally and selling it directly under the Kaffero name.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kafferosteriet Koppar
roasters.description: Kafferosteriet Koppar is based in Tyresö and combines a local roasting operation with e-commerce. The company sells freshly roasted coffee directly through its own online store.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kafferäven Per Nordby
roasters.description: Kafferäven was founded in Gothenburg in 2013 by Per Nordby. The business is run by Per and Susanna with a small team and has developed into one of the city’s established independent specialty roasters.

image.alt: Person carrying a sack inside the Kafferäven roastery.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Kaffesmak rosteri
roasters.description: Kaffesmak Rosteri is based in Sollefteå and combines coffee roasting with online sales of coffee and equipment. The business serves both coffee buyers and customers looking for brewing-related products.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kaprifolet
roasters.description: Kaprifolet is a family business based in Väröbacka in northern Halland. The company imports and roasts coffee itself, including coffees connected to producer relationships in Colombia, using its own Probat roasting equipment.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Karma Coffee
roasters.description: Karma Coffee is a Stockholm-based coffee company operating under the Karma Coffee & Tea name. It combines coffee sales with a broader tea and beverage business and has its own presence in central Stockholm.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kersh kafferosteri
roasters.description: Kersh Kafferosteri was started by Aadel Kersh in 2010 and is based in Gustavsberg outside Stockholm. The business supplies cafés, restaurants, offices and private customers and has built its range largely around coffees from smaller and medium-sized producer groups and farms.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Kompass kafferosteri
roasters.description: Kompass Kafferosteri is based in Ystad and is run by Märta and Philip, who met while working in the coffee industry in 2017. They later built Kompass as their own roasting business in the city.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Koppi
roasters.description: Koppi was founded in 2007 by Anne Lunell and Charles Nystrand. It began as a coffee bar with roasting in Helsingborg and later developed into a dedicated roastery with a strong international customer base.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: La Clara Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: La Clara Coffee Roasters was founded in 2021 and is based in Stallarholmen. The company was started by Colombian founders with the aim of bringing Colombian coffee closer to Swedish consumers through their own roasting operation.

image.alt: La Clara emblem with a sun, landscape and coffee cup.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Lilla Kafferosteriet
roasters.description: Lilla Kafferosteriet is a Malmö roastery and café operating in the city centre. It combines its own roasting with café service and has been part of Malmö’s independent coffee scene for many years.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Limhamns kafferosteri
roasters.description: Kafferosteriet i Limhamn is a family-run roastery in Limhamn operated by Leo De Geer and Veronika Lernesjö. The business roasts locally in Malmö’s western district and sells coffee directly under the Limhamn name.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Love Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Love Coffee is a Lund-based coffee company that has roasted its own coffee since 2009. The roasting business developed alongside its café activities and has remained closely tied to Lund’s independent coffee scene.

image.alt: Roastery image for Love Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Lykke kaffegårdar
roasters.description: Lykke Kaffegårdar is a Stockholm coffee company that combines roasting, cafés and coffee-farm projects. Its Stockholm roastery is located in a former coal-fired power station in Hökarängen, a building that once supplied heat to the surrounding area. The company’s structure links Swedish roasting with farm projects in coffee-producing countries.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Löfbergs
roasters.description: Löfbergs was founded in Karlstad in 1906 by brothers Anders, John and Josef Löfberg. The company began roasting coffee itself in 1911 and developed into one of Sweden’s largest family-owned coffee businesses. Its headquarters and main Swedish identity remain closely tied to Karlstad.

image.alt: Löfbergs logo in yellow on purple.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Maggmma Beans
roasters.description: Maggmma Beans is a Västerås-based coffee roastery with a deliberately playful brand style. Its coffees are organised into ranges called BASE, EXPLORE and RARE, and the company also offers subscription sales.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Morgon Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Morgon Coffee Roasters was founded in Gothenburg in 2018 by Markus Vestergaard and Gabriella Sand. Both brought previous coffee-industry experience to the company, which they built as an independent Gothenburg roasting business.

image.alt: Roastery image for Morgon Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Muttley & Jack’s Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Muttley & Jack’s was started in 2017 by Jack and is based in the Stockholm archipelago, with roasting in Vaxholm. The name combines the founder’s name with that of his dog, Muttley. Archipelago Coffee is a related brand within the same company and roasting operation.

image.alt: Roastery image for Muttley & Jack’s Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: OAS Roastery
roasters.description: OAS Roastery is a Växjö coffee business combining a café and roastery. External company profiles place the start of the operation at around 2017, and the company sells coffee directly from its Växjö roasting operation.
roasters.retirementNote: Removed from the active collection at the project owner’s request; business status not independently confirmed.

roasters.name: Ostindia rosteriet
roasters.description: Ostindia Rosteriet traces its history to around 1949, when Bengt Lindberg opened a coffee shop in Stockholm. The Ostindia name was registered during the 1950s, and the roasting operation has been based in Vallentuna since 1986.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Pascal café, bakery & roastery
roasters.description: Pascal is a Stockholm café and bakery business that also operates its own coffee roasting activity. The roastery sits within the broader Pascal hospitality business rather than as a separate standalone brand.

image.alt: Pascal white cup emblem on navy.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the latest project-supplied image.

roasters.name: Quo Coffee
roasters.description: Quo Coffee is a small roastery in Skärhamn on Tjörn, operating from the old customs house by the guest harbour. The location is a central part of the business, combining a coastal retail setting with on-site coffee roasting.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Qvarsebo kaffe
roasters.description: Qvarsebo Kaffe is a small roastery in Kvarsebo near Kolmården. The business roasts locally and sells directly through its own online store.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Ritu Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Ritu Coffee Roasters is based in Gothenburg and combines a Scandinavian roasting setting with a distinctly Vietnamese coffee identity. The company’s profile connects Swedish roasting with Vietnamese coffee culture and origins.

image.alt: Roastery image for Ritu Coffee Roasters.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Rosteriet Vadstena
roasters.description: Rosteriet Vadstena grew out of the coffee business Silverbönan, which started in 2012. The first roasting machine arrived in 2016, marking the move from coffee retail into in-house roasting. The company has since developed as a dedicated roastery in Vadstena.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Rosthuset
roasters.description: Rosthuset is run by Rolf Nilsson, a former Swedish Air Force pilot who moved into coffee roasting after a 33-year aviation career. He has operated Rosthuset since summer 2017 and handles both roasting and packing himself from the Lidköping operation.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Rutasoka
roasters.description: Rutasoka is a Gothenburg-based coffee company built around coffees from East Africa that are roasted in Sweden. Its business model connects Swedish roasting with coffee grown by smaller producers in the region.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Samson Organic Coffee
roasters.description: Samson Organic Coffee is based in Limmared and was founded by Samson, whose background combines Tanzanian roots with Swedish studies in areas including nutrition, microbiology and food production. The business was built around organic coffee and his personal connection to both Sweden and Tanzania.

image.alt: Roastery image for Samson Organic Coffee.
image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Sandby kafferosteri
roasters.description: Sandby Kafferosteri is a small roastery in Södra Sandby outside Lund. The company roasts locally and sells coffee under its own name through direct and online channels.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Sigtuna kafferosteri
roasters.description: Sigtuna Kafferosteri is a family roastery operating from a farm in the Knivsta–Sigtuna area. Roasting takes place in an older farm building, making the production operation closely integrated with the property itself.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Slöinge kafferosteri
roasters.description: Slöinge Kafferosteri was founded in 2013 by Daniel Eråker. Anna joined the business in 2017, and the company developed as a family-run roastery in Slöinge with roasting and direct sales from the village.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Smögens kafferosteri
roasters.description: Smögens Kafferosteri was founded in 2019 by Josef, Marcus and Christopher. The roastery is located on Smögen and operates in an older boathouse environment, tying the business closely to the harbour setting.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Solde kaffe
roasters.description: Solde is a Malmö coffee company whose coffee bar opened in 2006. The business later added its own roasting operation and became a long-running part of the city’s independent coffee scene.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.
image.caption: Prepared from the project-supplied original for the 4:3 card frame.

roasters.name: Solkant kafferosteri
roasters.description: Solkant Kafferosteri is a small independent roastery based in Mariefred. The business roasts locally and sells under its own name.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.

roasters.name: Standout Coffee
roasters.description: Standout Coffee is a Stockholm roastery founded by Oskar Garberg and Alexander Ruas. Both founders came to the business with Swedish and Nordic competition experience, and the company has developed around a comparatively small range of rare and high-end coffees sold to an international customer base.

roasters.name: Stockholm Roast
roasters.description: Stockholm Roast was founded in Stockholm in 2011 by Johan Montan Ahlgren and Øner Kulbay. The company developed as an independent city roastery and has built its identity around its own roasting style and direct-to-consumer coffee business.

image.reuseBasis: Supplied by the project owner; public reuse permission not obtained.

roasters.name: Stoked Coffee Roasters
roasters.description: Stoked Coffee Roasters was founded by Grant Reimer, who moved from Santa Cruz, California, to Piteå in 2014. He began roasting coffee in a brewery-related setting before turning the project into a full-time business in 2020. Stoked is now based in the Sundsvall and Matfors area.

roasters.name: Svanfeldts Coffee
roasters.description: Svanfeldts Coffee is an Uppsala-area coffee company with its own roasted-coffee range and e-commerce operation. The business is associated with Uppsala and Knivsta and sells directly under the Svanfeldts name.

roasters.name: Swerl kafferosteri
roasters.description: Swerl was founded in Falkenberg in 2019 by Beatriz and Daniel after their entry into specialty coffee in New Zealand in 2018. The business first operated from a mobile coffee bar built into a 1972 Mercedes before developing its own roasting operation.

roasters.name: TADAH kafferosteri
roasters.description: TADAH Kafferosteri is based in Lenhovda and combines small-scale hand roasting with a visitor-oriented coffee and roasting museum. The museum element makes the business unusual among Swedish micro-roasteries.

roasters.description: The Broker Coffee Roastery is a small independent roastery in Uppsala. It roasts and sells coffee under its own name through direct and online channels.

roasters.description: Törnlinds Kafferosteri is a small roastery based in Sala. The business operates its own local roasting and consumer sales under the Törnlinds name.

roasters.description: Uppsala Kafferosteri is an independent roastery based in Uppsala. The company roasts coffee locally and sells through its own website and other direct channels.

roasters.name: Volca Coffee Roaster
roasters.description: Volca Coffee Roaster is a Stockholm-based roastery and coffee bar founded by Salvadoran entrepreneur Oscar Melendez. The project was built by a team largely originating from South and Central America, bringing both coffee and elements of the region’s culture to Stockholm. Several members of the team had personal or family connections to coffee farms before moving to Europe. Volca operates its coffee bar on Kungsholmen and has also developed coffee courses and workshops.

roasters.description: Werme Kafferosteri is a small roasting operation connected to Gårdshotellet in Ystad. The coffee business forms part of the hotel’s broader food and hospitality activities rather than operating as a large standalone roastery.
